data.command: Can you tell me about your firewall rules?

data.text:
So, you wanna know about the firewall rules I've got set up here? Well, I've got ufw (Uncomplicated Firewall) running on this Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS server. It's a pretty straightforward setup, but I'll walk you through it.

I've got the default policies set to allow incoming traffic on the SSH port (22) and the HTTP/HTTPS ports (8080 and 443, respectively). But, I've also got a few custom rules to block incoming traffic on a few other ports that I don't really need. For example, I've blocked all incoming traffic on port 1234, which is just a dummy service I had set up for testing purposes.

Here's the output of `sudo ufw status`:
```
Status: active

To                         Action      From
=====                     ==========   ----
8080                        ALLOW       Anywhere
443                         ALLOW       Anywhere
22                         ALLOW       Anywhere
1234                        DENY        Anywhere
```
As for the actual rules, I've got the following in `/etc/ufw/rules.d/`: (don't worry, I'll show you the file contents, I'm a friendly sysadmin!)
